display_title: DIGITAL-ECCC-2027-DEPLOY-CYBER-11-CYBERAI Cybersecure tools, technologies and services relying on AI – Digital Europe Programme
call_title: Strengthening European Cybersecurity Technologies, Capacities and Preparedness (DIGITAL-ECCC-2027-DEPLOY-CYBER-11)
call_module_title: DIGITAL-ECCC-2027-DEPLOY-CYBER-11-CYBERAI Cybersecure tools, technologies and services relying on AI
executive_summary: Funds the development and deployment of AI-based cybersecurity systems, tools and services (threat and anomaly detection, including in operational technology, cyber threat intelligence, incident response, self-healing, vulnerability management, and risk reduction where AI, IoT and smart grids cross over) for Cyber Hubs, CSIRTs, competent authorities and NIS 2 entities. Any public or private legal entity established in an EU or EEA country and not controlled from outside them may apply, alone or in a consortium. Simple Grants at a 50% funding rate; EU contribution expected at EUR 3–5 million per project, EUR 15 million for about 4 projects; indicative duration 36 months. Opened 1 September 2026; single-stage deadline 14 January 2027, 17:00 CET.
status_rationale: The call document (DEP 11, pp. 11-14, CYBERAI Objectives and Scope) funds AI-based cybersecurity tools and services, including anomaly detection in Operational Technology infrastructures and risk reduction in the crossover between AI, IoT and smart grids, with NIS 2 entities and the private sector among the targeted stakeholders. This touches TenneT's need to secure its control systems as a critical-infrastructure operator, close to TwinEU (grid resilience and cybersecurity) and, more loosely, to the AI and digital twin work of GNN4GC and the Digital Twin Programme. Section 6 (pp. 48-50) admits any legal entity established in and controlled from an EU or EEA country as a beneficiary, with no consortium minimum, so TenneT TSO B.V. could be a funded partner at the 50% Simple Grant rate, for example as the operator that validates the tools in its environment. A funded partner role fits C1.3.
